name: Aliağa
title: Aliağa Ship UTM | Gas Carriers, Tankers and Scrap Bulkers
description: UTM at Aliağa and Nemrut Bay: thickness gauging of ballast tanks, decks, piping and hatch covers on LNG and LPG carriers, tankers and scrap bulk carriers.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ships at Aliağa's Gas, Refinery and Scrap Terminals
intro: Aliağa, on the Aegean coast north of Izmir, is a working industrial port: LNG carriers discharge into a floating regasification unit, tankers serve the refineries and the petrochemical complex, bulk carriers deliver scrap to the steel mills, and ships at the end of their lives are dismantled in its recycling yards. For a trading ship the gauging windows come from cargo calls and anchorage waits. Technicians travel from India to join each vessel, with the plan agreed with the terminal before the ship berths.

highlights.h: LNG carriers at the Etki FSRU
highlights.p: LNG carriers discharge into the floating storage and regasification unit at the Etki terminal by ship-to-ship transfer. Machinery-space piping, certified ballast tanks and deck structure outside the hazardous zones can be gauged during the call, within the terminal's rules.

Repeated scrap cargoes punish hatch covers and coamings as well as holds. Measuring cover top plates, skirts and coaming plating after discharge shows whether weathertightness problems come from wastage or from mechanical damage, before the ship loads its next cargo.

Ships waiting for an Aliağa berth, or for orders after discharging, lie at anchor off the coast. A bulk carrier in ballast or a tanker between cargoes can have ballast tanks and empty holds gauged there for a buyer or ahead of a docking.

port.h: Aliağa: an industrial coast between Izmir and Çandarlı Bay
p: Aliağa occupies the Aegean coast north of the Gulf of Izmir, a district built around industry rather than around a city harbour. Its shoreline runs from Nemrut Bay, lined with container, bulk and liquid terminals, past the refinery and petrochemical jetties to the LNG terminal in Horozgediği bay near the village of Çakmaklı, on the south-western side of Çandarlı Bay. Ship movements are overseen by the Aliağa harbour master and by the vessel traffic service sector covering these waters, and pilotage is compulsory at the LNG terminal. The coast faces west into the Aegean, so the strong northerlies of summer and the southerly gales of winter both affect berthing and launch work, although the bays give some shelter and most terminals lie inside them rather than on the open coast.

The district's trades follow its industry. Two refineries and the Petkim petrochemical works bring crude, product and chemical tankers and LPG carriers; the electric-arc steel mills import scrap in Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers and ship out finished steel; the Nemrut Bay terminals handle containers and general cargo; and gas arrives as LNG for the national grid, both through the floating unit and at an onshore import terminal. LNG carriers discharging at the Etki terminal transfer their cargo ship to ship into the moored FSRU, at a berth designed for carriers up to Q-Flex size, so the port sees modern gas carriers as well as older dry bulk tonnage, often within the same week. Each of those ship types has a different set of spaces that can realistically be opened during its call.

Aliağa is also the centre of Turkish ship recycling. A row of recycling yards on this coast dismantles ships brought in for demolition, and the steel recovered from them goes to the same mills that import scrap by sea. The European Commission's February 2025 update of the European List counted eleven facilities in Türkiye, which matters to owners of EU-flagged ships and to any seller whose contract names a listed yard. For a ship that is still trading, the recycling zone is mostly background, but it brings sale brokers, cash buyers and recycling paperwork into the local conversation, and it means the ships calling here range from new LNG carriers to tonnage in its final years, with very different inspection needs.

facilities.h: Gauging locations along the Aliağa coast
p: At the LNG terminal, work is limited by the terminal's hazardous-area rules and by the fact that the carrier lies outboard of the FSRU during transfer. Certified ballast tanks, engine-room sea-water and cooling piping, accommodation and deck structure away from the cargo manifold are the realistic targets, and berthing takes place in daylight only, which sets when the team can board. At the refinery and Petkim jetties a similar logic applies to tankers and LPG carriers, with ballast tanks entered only once certified and released by the master. At the scrap berths, discharge by grab and magnet frees holds one at a time, and hatch covers can be measured while they are open for discharge.

There is no large docking yard at Aliağa, so ships that need steel renewal go north to the Marmara yards at Tuzla and Yalova, or to repair yards in Greece and further afield. Gauging done here becomes the pre-docking record, and we send it to the chosen yard with each location referenced to the ship's drawings. Ships waiting at anchor for a berth, or for orders after discharge, can be boarded by launch from the port, which suits a buyer's inspection of a bulk carrier in ballast or a ballast-tank programme on a tanker between cargoes.
list: Etki LNG terminal near Çakmaklı — ballast tank, machinery-space piping and deck structure gauging on LNG carriers during ship-to-ship discharge, within terminal rules.
Refinery and Petkim jetties — deck, piping and certified ballast space readings on crude, product and chemical tankers and LPG carriers.
Scrap and steel berths — hold, hatch cover and coaming gauging on bulk carriers as each hold is discharged.
Nemrut Bay container and general cargo terminals — deck, coaming and ballast tank checks during port stays.
Anchorages off Aliağa — pre-purchase or pre-docking gauging on ships waiting for berths or orders.

context.h: Port state control, gas terminals and ship recycling rules at Aliağa
p: Turkey participates in both the Mediterranean MoU and the Black Sea MoU, and port state control at Aliağa sees an unusually wide range of ships, from modern LNG carriers to elderly scrap carriers in the regional trade. On the bulk side, hatch covers, coamings, air pipe heads and hold structure are frequent findings, while tankers and gas carriers draw attention to deck piping, fire mains and ballast tank condition. Gas and refinery terminals add their own acceptance checks before a ship berths, so a superintendent with doubts about a fire main or a ballast tank is better placed if the readings are already on file.

Ship recycling regulation forms the backdrop. EU-flagged ships must be recycled at yards on the European List under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, and the February 2025 update included eleven facilities in Türkiye; the list changes, so check the current version before relying on it. The Hong Kong Convention has also been in force internationally since June 2025. Both regimes rest on an Inventory of Hazardous Materials kept up to date through a ship's life, and ships calling at EU ports need one whatever their flag. None of that is thickness measurement, but a ship with a current, credible condition record is easier to sell for further trading than one whose structure is an unknown.

psc: Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU

jobs.p: Jobs at Aliağa are fitted around cargo operations and the terminals' safety rules. Gas carrier managers ask for ballast tank and machinery-space piping readings during a discharge; tanker superintendents use refinery calls to start vetting or survey preparation; bulk carrier owners in the scrap trade want hatch covers, coamings and holds checked between cargoes; and buyers inspect ships waiting at anchor. Because the nearest docking yards are some way off, many programmes are pre-docking estimates sent on to the yard before the ship sails. Each scope is agreed with the terminal, the master and the agent before arrival, since access rules differ from jetty to jetty.
list: Ballast tank and engine-room sea-water piping gauging on an LNG carrier during its ship-to-ship discharge at the Etki terminal.
Hatch cover top plate, skirt and coaming gauging on a Handysize scrap carrier after discharge, following repeated weathertightness complaints.
Deck and cargo piping readings on an LPG carrier at a Petkim jetty ahead of its intermediate survey.
Pre-purchase gauging of a Supramax at the Aliağa anchorage for a buyer intending to keep it trading.
Pre-docking steel estimate on a chemical tanker before it sails for a Tuzla yard.

logistics: The team lands at Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport, normally after connecting in Istanbul, and reaches Aliağa by the coast road or on the İZBAN suburban line, which runs north from Izmir to Aliağa. Terminal permits, ISPS passes and launch bookings for anchorage boarding come through the ship's agent, and the LNG terminal and refinery jetties expect personnel and equipment details well before arrival. Technicians travelling from India need Turkish visas, so we start applications when a likely call is identified and keep them valid across the ship's expected window.

faqs.q: Can an LNG carrier be gauged during its discharge at the Etki terminal?
faqs.a: Partly. During ship-to-ship transfer into the FSRU, cargo containment and the manifold area are off-limits, but ballast tanks certified for entry, engine-room and sea-water piping, and deck structure outside hazardous zones can usually be measured. The terminal berths ships in daylight only, and instruments must be acceptable for the zone they are used in, so the programme is agreed with the terminal and the master before the call.

faqs.q: Why measure hatch covers on scrap carriers?
faqs.a: Because scrap cargoes damage them. Heavy, irregular pieces dropped by magnet and grab dent cover panels and coamings, and repeated impacts break the coating and start corrosion along skirts and coaming tops. Measuring cover top plates, skirt plates and coaming plating tells the superintendent whether leaks come from wastage or from deformation, which decides whether the fix is renewal or straightening.

faqs.q: Where do ships calling at Aliağa go for a docking?
faqs.a: Usually to the Marmara yards at Tuzla and Yalova, or to repair yards in Greece and further afield, since Aliağa has no large docking facility of its own. Measuring during a cargo call here lets the chosen yard receive a steel renewal estimate before the ship arrives, and the same measurement points are then checked again in dock.

faqs.q: Do the refinery and petrochemical jetties allow gauging during cargo work?
faqs.a: Within limits. Terminals at Aliağa apply their own permit-to-work and hazardous-area rules, so instruments, work locations and timing are agreed beforehand through the agent. Deck plating, deck piping, the fire main and ballast tanks released by the master are normally possible; cargo tanks are not entered while the ship is handling cargo. Larger programmes are split between the call and the next docking.
